title: Dropping Values vs References
goal: Distinguish between dropping owned values and dropping references.
hints: References do not own the value they point to.
`std::mem::drop` on a reference only drops the reference, which does nothing.
explanation: `std::mem::drop(h)` takes ownership of `h` and drops it immediately, setting `DROPPED` to `true`. Passing `&h` only drops the borrow reference, leaving `h` alive until function exit so `DROPPED` remains `false`. `h.drop()` fails with `E0040`.
